Let $A$ be a square complex matrix
whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite type $n$. Then there are unitary matrices $U$ and $V$
and nonnegative real numbers $\sigma_i$ for $i \in n$ such that, writing $D$ for the diagonal
matrix with diagonal entries $\sigma_i$ and $V^*$ for the conjugate transpose of $V$, we have
$A = U D V^*$.

## Sources

- R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013).

articles.title: Unitary reduction of a complex matrix to rectangular diagonal form
articles.statement:
Every rectangular complex matrix becomes rectangular diagonal after a unitary
change of basis on the right, with a further unitary change of basis on the
codomain (S. Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed., Section 7E).

articles.title: Complex SVD with nonincreasing singular values
articles.statement:
This is the rectangular complex SVD with singular values in nonincreasing order.

Proof: Multiply the rectangular-diagonal factorization on the right by `Vᴴ`.

articles.title: Real singular value decomposition
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a real $m \times n$ matrix. Then there are
orthogonal matrices $U$ of size $m \times m$ and $V$ of size $n \times n$ and real numbers
$\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_n \ge 0$ with $\sigma_j = 0$ for every $j > m$, such that
$A = U \Sigma V^{\mathsf{T}}$, where $\Sigma$ is the $m \times n$ matrix with
$\Sigma_{jj} = \sigma_j$ for $j \le \min(m, n)$ and all other entries zero.

Proof: apply the spectral theorem to $A^{\mathsf{T}} A$, normalize the images under $A$ of the
eigenvectors with positive eigenvalues, and extend them to an orthonormal basis of
$\mathbb{R}^m$, as in the proof of S. Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed., 7.70, and the
matrix form that follows it (Section 7E).

## Sources

- G. H. Golub and C. F. Van Loan, Matrix Computations, 4th ed., Johns Hopkins University Press (2013), Theorem 2.4.1.

articles.title: Squared Frobenius norm as the sum of squared singular values
articles.statement:
Frobenius-norm identity for an SVD: the sum of the squared singular values is
the sum of the squared norms of the entries.

articles.title: Monotonicity of the determinant on the positive semidefinite cone
articles.statement:
**Monotonicity of the determinant on the positive semidefinite
cone**: if `S` and `D - S` are positive semidefinite, then
`det S ≤ det D`.

articles.title: Equality case of Fischer's inequality
articles.statement:
For `A` and `D`
positive definite and `[[A, B], [Bᴴ, D]]` positive semidefinite,
`det [[A, B], [Bᴴ, D]] = det A * det D` iff `B = 0`.

articles.title: Fischer's determinant inequality
articles.statement:
For a positive semidefinite
block matrix `[[A, B], [Bᴴ, D]]` with real entries,
`det [[A, B], [Bᴴ, D]] ≤ det A * det D`.

articles.title: Determinant at least one when W minus identity is positive semidefinite
articles.statement:
If `W - 1` is positive semidefinite, then `1 ≤ det W`, since every
eigenvalue of `W` is at least `1`.

articles.title: Equality in the AM–GM bound for the determinant
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a positive
semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then $(\operatorname{Re} \det A)^{1/n} =
\operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{tr} A)/n$ if and only if $A = cI$ for some real number $c \ge 0$,
where $I$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix.

articles.title: AM–GM inequality for the determinant of a positive semidefinite matrix, power form
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then
$\operatorname{Re} \det A \le (\operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{tr} A)/n)^n$.

articles.title: Hadamard's inequality for positive semidefinite matrices
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a positive
semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then the real part of the determinant of $A$ is at most
the product of the real parts of its diagonal entries:
$\operatorname{Re} \det A \le \prod_{i=1}^{n} \operatorname{Re} A_{ii}$.

articles.title: AM–GM inequality for the determinant of a positive semidefinite matrix
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$
and let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then
$(\operatorname{Re} \det A)^{1/n} \le \operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{tr} A)/n$.

This is the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality for the eigenvalues of $A$.

articles.title: Hadamard's determinant inequality
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and every $n \times n$
complex matrix $A = (a_{ij})$,

$$|\det A| \le \prod_{i=1}^{n} \Big( \sum_{j=1}^{n} |a_{ij}|^2 \Big)^{1/2},$$

that is, the absolute value of the determinant of $A$ is at most the product of the Euclidean
lengths of its rows.

## Sources

- J. Hadamard, Résolution d'une question relative aux déterminants, Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques 17 (1893), 240–246.

articles.title: The trace of a product of positive semidefinite matrices has nonnegative real part
articles.statement:
Let
$A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrices. Then the real part of the
trace of $AB$ is nonnegative: $\operatorname{Re} \operatorname{tr}(AB) \ge 0$.

articles.title: Hoffman–Wielandt inequality for Hermitian matrices
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian
$n \times n$ complex matrices with eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_n$ and
$\mu_1 \ge \dots \ge \mu_n$ respectively, counted with multiplicity. Then
$\sum_{i=1}^n (\lambda_i - \mu_i)^2 \le \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^n |A_{ij} - B_{ij}|^2$, that is,
the left side is at most the squared Frobenius norm of $A - B$.

## Sources

- A. J. Hoffman and H. W. Wielandt, Duke Math. J. 20 (1953), DOI 10.1215/S0012-7094-53-02004-3.

articles.title: Lidskii's inequality
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian complex square matrices indexed by a
finite set with $N$ elements. List the eigenvalues of $A$, of $B$ and of $B - A$, each with
multiplicity and in decreasing order, as $\alpha_1 \ge \dots \ge \alpha_N$,
$\beta_1 \ge \dots \ge \beta_N$ and $\gamma_1 \ge \dots \ge \gamma_N$. Then for every real
$p \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{j=1}^N |\alpha_j - \beta_j|^p \le \sum_{j=1}^N |\gamma_j|^p.$$

## Sources

- V. B. Lidskii, On the proper values of a sum and product of symmetric matrices, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 75 (1950), 769-772. Listed as an additional statement of §99 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `lidskii_inequality` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Lidskii–Last theorem
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian complex square matrices indexed by a
finite set with $N$ elements, and list the eigenvalues of $A$ and of $B$, each with multiplicity
and in decreasing order, as $\alpha_1 \ge \dots \ge \alpha_N$ and $\beta_1 \ge \dots \ge \beta_N$.
Then

$$\sum_{j=1}^N |\alpha_j - \beta_j| \le \sum_{i,j} |A_{ij} - B_{ij}|.$$

## Sources

- V. B. Lidskii (1950); the entrywise ℓ¹ form is due to Y. Last (around 1993). Listed as §99 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `lidskii_last` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Log-determinant trace inequality
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be positive definite real square
matrices indexed by a finite set with $n$ elements. Then
$\log(\det A \cdot \det B) \le \operatorname{tr}(AB) - n$.

The eigenvalues $\lambda$ of the positive definite matrix $B^{1/2} A B^{1/2}$, where $B^{1/2}$ is
the positive semidefinite square root of $B$, satisfy $\log \lambda \le \lambda - 1$; this
matrix has determinant $\det A \det B$ and trace $\operatorname{tr}(AB)$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of the determinant on the positive semidefinite cone
articles.statement: `det B ≤ det (A + B)` for `A` and `B` positive semidefinite.

articles.title: Minkowski's determinant inequality
articles.statement:
For positive semidefinite
`A` and `B`,
`(det (A + B)) ^ (1 / n) ≥ (det A) ^ (1 / n) + (det B) ^ (1 / n)`.

articles.title: Positive definiteness of a block matrix via the Schur complement
articles.statement:
A block matrix with a positive definite top-left block and a positive
definite Schur complement is positive definite. This is the one-step
induction step of Sylvester's criterion, stated for a `1 × 1`
bottom-right block.

articles.title: Full leading principal submatrix is the matrix itself
articles.statement: The full leading principal submatrix is the matrix itself.

articles.title: Leading principal submatrix
articles.statement:
The leading `k × k` principal submatrix of `A`: the submatrix on the
first `k` rows and columns.

articles.title: Sylvester's criterion
articles.statement:
A Hermitian real matrix is positive
definite if and only if all of its leading principal minors are
positive. The Hermitian hypothesis is essential: `!![1, 2; 0, 1]` has
leading minors `1` and `1` but is not Hermitian, hence not positive
definite.

articles.title: Linear functionals on doubly stochastic matrices are bounded below at a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $P$ be a doubly stochastic real $I \times I$ matrix (its entries are
nonnegative and each of its rows and columns sums to $1$), and let $c_{ij} \in \mathbb{R}$ for
$i, j \in I$. Then there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $I$ with
$\sum_i c_{i \sigma(i)} \le \sum_i \sum_j c_{ij} P_{ij}$. That is, the linear functional
$M \mapsto \sum_{i, j} c_{ij} M_{ij}$ takes a value at some permutation matrix that is at most its
value at $P$.

The proof uses Birkhoff's theorem.

articles.title: A pairing of eigenvalues bounds the trace of a product from below
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
real symmetric matrices with rows and columns indexed by a finite set $I$, and let
$(\alpha_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(\beta_i)_{i \in I}$ be their eigenvalues, listed with multiplicity.
Then there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $I$ with
$\sum_i \alpha_i \beta_{\sigma(i)} \le \operatorname{tr}(AB)$.

This is the lower half of von Neumann's trace inequality, in pairing form.

articles.title: A pairing of eigenvalues bounds the trace of a product from above
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
real symmetric matrices with rows and columns indexed by a finite set $I$, and let
$(\alpha_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(\beta_i)_{i \in I}$ be their eigenvalues, listed with multiplicity.
Then there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $I$ with
$\operatorname{tr}(AB) \le \sum_i \alpha_i \beta_{\sigma(i)}$.

This is the upper half of von Neumann's trace inequality, in pairing form.

articles.title: The quadratic form of a symmetric matrix in an orthonormal eigenbasis
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be a real
symmetric matrix with rows and columns indexed by a finite set $I$, and let $(v_j)_{j \in I}$ be
the orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^I$ of eigenvectors of $B$ chosen by the spectral theorem,
with $B v_j = \beta_j v_j$. Then for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^I$,
$\langle x, Bx \rangle = \sum_j \beta_j \langle v_j, x \rangle^2$.

articles.title: The overlap matrix of two orthonormal bases is doubly stochastic
articles.statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set
and let $(u_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(v_j)_{j \in I}$ be orthonormal bases of $\mathbb{R}^I$ with its
standard inner product. Then the $I \times I$ matrix with entries
$P_{ij} = \langle v_j, u_i \rangle^2$ is doubly stochastic: its entries are nonnegative and each
of its rows and columns sums to $1$.

articles.title: The trace of a product of symmetric matrices in their eigenbases
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be real
symmetric matrices with rows and columns indexed by a finite set $I$. Let $(u_i)_{i \in I}$ and
$(v_j)_{j \in I}$ be the orthonormal bases of $\mathbb{R}^I$ of eigenvectors of $A$ and $B$ chosen
by the spectral theorem, with $A u_i = \alpha_i u_i$ and $B v_j = \beta_j v_j$. Then
$\operatorname{tr}(AB) = \sum_i \sum_j \alpha_i \beta_j \langle v_j, u_i \rangle^2$.

articles.title: Exponential-sum formula for circulant eigenvalues
articles.statement: The canonical DFT definition agrees with the original negative-exponent eigenvalue sum.

articles.title: Zeroth circulant eigenvalue is the sum of entries
articles.statement: The Fourier eigenvalue at `j = 0` is the sum of the entries of `v`.

articles.title: Fourier eigenvalue of a circulant matrix
articles.statement: The `j`-th Fourier eigenvalue of a circulant matrix is its canonical DFT.

articles.title: Circulant matrices are diagonalized by the Fourier matrix
articles.statement: Circulant matrices are diagonalized by the Fourier matrix.

articles.title: Fourier vectors are eigenvectors of circulant matrices
articles.statement: Every Fourier vector is an eigenvector of every circulant matrix.

articles.title: Determinant of a circulant matrix
articles.statement: The determinant of a circulant matrix is the product of its Fourier eigenvalues.

articles.title: Entrywise exponential formula for the Fourier matrix
articles.statement: The Fourier matrix agrees entrywise with its original exponential formula.

articles.title: Entrywise exponential formula for the inverse Fourier matrix
articles.statement: The inverse Fourier matrix agrees entrywise with its original exponential formula.

articles.title: Inverse Fourier matrix acts as the DFT divided by n
articles.statement: Inverse Fourier matrix multiplication is the canonical DFT divided by `n`.

articles.title: Inverse Fourier matrix
articles.statement: The inverse Fourier matrix, `(1 / n)` times the negative standard character.

articles.title: Fourier matrix times its inverse is the identity
articles.statement: The Fourier matrix is invertible, with inverse `fourierMatrixInv`.

articles.title: Fourier matrix acts as n times the inverse DFT
articles.statement: Fourier matrix multiplication is the canonical inverse DFT multiplied by `n`.

articles.title: Fourier matrix
articles.statement: The Fourier matrix, whose `j`-th column is the standard character `fourierVec n j`.

articles.title: Exponential formula for Fourier vectors
articles.statement: The character definition of a Fourier vector agrees with its exponential formula.

articles.title: Fourier vector on the integers modulo n
articles.statement: The `j`-th Fourier vector on `ZMod n`, using the canonical positive character.

articles.title: Two-dimensional block-circulant matrix on the torus
articles.statement: The block-circulant matrix on `(ℤ_L × ℤ_L) × Fin d` with block `v (p - q)` in position `(p, q)`.

articles.title: Block-circulant matrix over ℤ_n
articles.statement: The block-circulant matrix on `ℤ_n × Fin d` with block `v (p - q)` in position `(p, q)`.

articles.title: Fourier symbol of a two-dimensional block-circulant matrix
articles.statement: The Fourier symbol `∑_k ω ^ (k₁ j₁ + k₂ j₂) • v k` at frequency `j`.

articles.title: Fourier symbol of a block-circulant matrix
articles.statement: The Fourier symbol `∑_k ω ^ (k j) • v k` of a block-circulant matrix at frequency `j`.

articles.title: Sum of the eigenvalues of a circulant matrix
articles.statement: The Fourier eigenvalues sum to `n * v 0`.

articles.title: Standard root of unity as the standard additive character
articles.statement: For nonzero `n`, `zeta n` is the canonical standard character at `1`.

articles.title: $e^{2\pi i/n}$ is a primitive n-th root of unity
articles.statement: For nonzero `n`, the exponential is a primitive `n`-th root of unity.

articles.title: Standard primitive n-th root of unity $e^{2\pi i/n}$
articles.statement:
The exponential `exp (2 * π * I / n)`, a primitive `n`-th root for nonzero `n`.
This definition is total: at `n = 0`, it is `exp 0 = 1`.

articles.title: Hadamard matrices with circulant core: Paley and twin-prime cases
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural
number such that either $n$ is a prime with $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, or $n = p(p + 2)$ for some
natural number $p$ with $p$ and $p + 2$ both prime. Then there is an $(n + 1) \times (n + 1)$
Hadamard matrix $H$ with integer entries, rows and columns indexed by $0, 1, \dots, n$ (so every
entry of $H$ is $1$ or $-1$ and $H^{\mathsf T} H = (n + 1) I$), that has a circulant core: there
is a function $v \colon \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $H_{i+1, j+1} = v(i - j)$ for
all $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, where $i - j$ is taken modulo $n$.

articles.title: Circulant-core Hadamard matrices with orthogonal rows and columns
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural
number such that either $n$ is a prime with $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, or $n = p(p + 2)$ for some
natural number $p$ with $p$ and $p + 2$ both prime. Then there is an $(n + 1) \times (n + 1)$
integer matrix $H$, with rows and columns indexed by $0, 1, \dots, n$, such that every entry of
$H$ is $1$ or $-1$, $H H^{\mathsf T} = (n + 1) I$ and $H^{\mathsf T} H = (n + 1) I$, and there
is a function $v \colon \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ such that the submatrix
$(H_{i+1, j+1})_{0 \le i, j \le n - 1}$ obtained by deleting row $0$ and column $0$ equals the
circulant matrix of $v$, whose $(i, j)$ entry is $v(i - j)$ with $i - j$ taken modulo $n$.

articles.title: A circulant core is a circulant submatrix
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $H$ be an
$(n + 1) \times (n + 1)$ integer matrix with rows and columns indexed by $0, 1, \dots, n$. Then
$H$ has a circulant core, meaning that there is a function
$v \colon \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $H_{i+1, j+1} = v(i - j)$ for all
$i, j \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, if and only if there is a function
$v \colon \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ such that the submatrix
$(H_{i+1, j+1})_{0 \le i, j \le n - 1}$ equals the circulant matrix of $v$, whose $(i, j)$
entry is $v(i - j)$. In both conditions $i - j$ is taken modulo $n$.

articles.title: One-sided orthogonality characterizes Hadamard matrices
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a natural number and
let $H$ be an $m \times m$ integer matrix. Then every entry of $H$ is $1$ or $-1$ and
$H^{\mathsf T} H = m I$ if and only if every entry of $H$ is a unitary element of $\mathbb{Z}$
(that is, $1$ or $-1$), $H H^{\mathsf T} = m I$ and $H^{\mathsf T} H = m I$. The right-hand side
is the general notion of a Hadamard matrix, with entries unitary and $H H^{*} = H^{*} H = m I$;
over $\mathbb{Z}$ the conjugate transpose $H^{*}$ is the transpose.

articles.title: Hadamard matrix
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$, an $m \times m$ matrix $H$ with integer
entries is a Hadamard matrix when every entry of $H$ is $1$ or $-1$ and
$H^{\mathsf T} H = m I$, where $I$ is the $m \times m$ identity matrix.

This predicate is used for Hadamard matrices of order $n + 1$ with circulant core, which exist
when $n$ is a prime congruent to $3$ mod $4$ (Paley) or $n = p(p + 2)$ with $p$ and $p + 2$
both prime (Stanton–Sprott/Whiteman).

## Sources

- Richard P. Brent and Adam B. Yedidia, "Computation of Maximal Determinants of Binary Circulant Matrices," Journal of Integer Sequences 21 (2018), Article 18.5.6, Theorem, lines 684–695, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL21/Brent/brent11.tex quoting Kotsireas et al.; attributions at lines 698–704. The prime-power versions of cases (1)–(2), if the source allows them, and cases (3)–(4) of the source theorem (Singer, Hall) are not part of this statement.

articles.title: Hadamard bound for zero-one determinants
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $B$ be an $n \times n$
real matrix each of whose entries is $0$ or $1$. Then

$$|\det B| \le 2^{-n} (n+1)^{(n+1)/2}.$$

The bound comes from bordering and signing $2B$ to obtain an $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix with
entries $\pm 1$ whose determinant is $2^n \det B$, and applying Hadamard's determinant inequality.

## Sources

- Richard P. Brent and Adam B. Yedidia, "Computation of Maximal Determinants of Binary Circulant Matrices," Journal of Integer Sequences 21 (2018), Article 18.5.6. https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL21/Brent/brent11.tex, lines 226–238.

articles.title: Finite Hankel matrix
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a sequence $s \colon \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$
with values in a set $\alpha$, the $n \times n$ Hankel matrix generated by $s$ has rows and columns
indexed by $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $(i, j)$ entry $s_{i+j}$, where $i + j$ is the sum in
$\mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Infinite Hankel matrix
articles.statement:
For a sequence $s \colon \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ with values in a
set $\alpha$, the infinite Hankel matrix generated by $s$ has rows and columns indexed by
$\mathbb{N}$ and $(i, j)$ entry $s_{i+j}$.

articles.title: Entries of the Hurwitz matrix
articles.statement:
For sequences $a, b \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative
ring $R$ and indices $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ (counted from zero), the Hurwitz entry $h_{ij}$ is $0$ if
$i \ge 2j + 2$; otherwise it is $a_{j - i/2}$ if $i$ is even and $b_{j - (i-1)/2}$ if $i$ is odd.

## Sources

- Barry's definition in the Journal of Integer Sequences, vol. 15.

articles.title: Hurwitz matrix
articles.statement:
For sequences $a, b \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative ring $R$ and
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hurwitz matrix of order $n$ is the $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix whose entry
in row $i$ and column $j$, for $0 \le i, j \le n$, is the Hurwitz entry $h_{ij}$ of $a$ and $b$.

articles.title: Hurwitz transform of a single sequence
articles.statement:
For a sequence $a \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a
commutative ring $R$, its Hurwitz transform is the Hurwitz transform of $a$ and the sequence
$(0^k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, which is $1$ at $k = 0$ and $0$ for $k \ge 1$.

articles.title: Hurwitz transform
articles.statement:
For sequences $a, b \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative ring $R$,
the Hurwitz transform of $a$ and $b$ is the sequence whose $n$-th term, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, is
the determinant of the Hurwitz matrix of $a$ and $b$ of order $n$.

articles.title: Inverse positivity of M-matrices
articles.statement:
The inverse of a nonsingular M-matrix is entrywise
nonnegative (Berman–Plemmons, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.3, (G20) ⇒ (N38)).

articles.title: Neumann series
articles.statement:
If `K` is entrywise nonnegative with spectral radius `< 1`, then
`(1 - K)⁻¹` is entrywise nonnegative (the proof identifies it with the limit of the partial
sums `∑_{n<N} Kⁿ`).

articles.title: Hurwitz matrix
articles.statement: A real square matrix is **Hurwitz** if every complex eigenvalue has negative real part.

articles.title: Nonsingular M-matrix
articles.statement:
A **nonsingular M-matrix** is a Z-matrix all of whose complex eigenvalues have positive
real part (Berman–Plemmons, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.3, condition (G20)).

articles.title: Invertibility of 1 − K when the spectral radius is below one
articles.statement:
If the spectral radius of `K` is `< 1`, then `1` is not an eigenvalue of `K`, so `1 - K`
is invertible.

articles.title: Nonsingular M-matrices are invertible
articles.statement: A nonsingular M-matrix is invertible.

articles.title: Z-matrix
articles.statement: A **Z-matrix** has nonpositive off-diagonal entries.

articles.title: Collatz–Wielandt lower bound
articles.statement:
If `K ≥ 0` entrywise, `z ≥ 0`, `z ≠ 0` and
`r • z ≤ K *ᵥ z` with `r ≥ 0`, then `r` is at most the spectral radius of `K`.

articles.title: Csima–Datta theorem
articles.statement:
For `0 < n`, a symmetric nonnegative matrix has a positive vector
`d` with `diag(d) A diag(d)` doubly stochastic if and only if it has total support.

articles.title: Csima–Datta: sufficiency of total support
articles.statement:
A symmetric nonnegative matrix with total
support has a positive vector `d` with `diag(d) A diag(d)` doubly stochastic.

## Sources

- Csima & Datta (1972); Sinkhorn & Knopp (1967).

articles.title: Sinkhorn's scaling theorem
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix all of
whose entries are strictly positive. Then there are vectors $r, c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with strictly
positive entries such that the matrix with entries $r_i A_{ij} c_j$ is doubly stochastic, that is,
its entries are nonnegative and each of its rows and each of its columns sums to $1$.

## Sources

- R. Sinkhorn, Ann. Math. Statist. 35 (1964), 876-879, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177703591.

articles.title: Corner entry of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers
with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$,
and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with
coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{2n-2,\,2n-1} = 1$.

articles.title: Finite support of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers
with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$,
and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with
coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{i,j} = 0$ for all $i, j$ with $i \ge 2n$ or
$j \ge 2n$.

articles.title: Interior recurrence of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers
with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$,
and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with
coefficients $\beta$. Then for all $i, j < 2n - 1$,
$S_{i,j} = \lambda S_{i+1,j+1} + \nu (S_{i+1,j} + S_{i,j+1})$.

articles.title: Nu-lambda Pascal matrix with coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with
$n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$.
An array $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ of complex numbers, indexed from $0$, is a
$(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$ when the following
hold: $S_{i,j} = 0$ whenever $i \ge 2n$ or $j \ge 2n$; $S_{i,j} = -S_{j,i}$ for all $i, j$;
$S_{2n-2,\,2n-1} = 1$; $S_{j,\,2n-1} = \sum_{t=0}^{N-1} \beta_t S_{j+t+1,\,2n-1}$ for every
$j < 2n - 2$; and $S_{i,j} = \lambda S_{i+1,j+1} + \nu (S_{i+1,j} + S_{i,j+1})$ for all
$i, j < 2n - 1$.

The definition also allows $N = 0$; then the sum is empty, so the entries $S_{j,\,2n-1}$
with $j < 2n - 2$ vanish. The intended coefficient families have $N > 0$.

articles.title: Last-column recurrence of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers
with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$,
and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with
coefficients $\beta$. Then for every $j < 2n - 2$,
$S_{j,\,2n-1} = \sum_{t=0}^{N-1} \beta_t S_{j+t+1,\,2n-1}$.

articles.title: Nu-lambda Pascal matrices are skew-symmetric
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers
with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$,
and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with
coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{i,j} = -S_{j,i}$ for all $i, j$.

articles.title: Perron–Frobenius theorem for nonzero irreducible nonnegative matrices
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero
real square matrix with rows and columns indexed by a nonempty finite set $S$, and suppose $A$ is
irreducible: its entries are nonnegative, and for all $i, j \in S$ there is a path
$i = i_0, i_1, \dots, i_k = j$ of length $k \ge 1$ with $A_{i_{t-1} i_t} > 0$ for every $t$. Then
there are a real number $r > 0$ and a vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^S$ with $v_i > 0$ for every
$i \in S$ such that $Av = rv$, and every complex number $\mu$ with
$\det(\mu E - A_{\mathbb{C}}) = 0$ satisfies $|\mu| \le r$, where $E$ is the identity matrix and
$A_{\mathbb{C}}$ is the complexification of $A$.

The hypothesis $A \ne 0$ is not needed: irreducibility already forces some entry to be positive.

## Sources

- O. Perron, Math. Ann. 64 (1907), 248-263, DOI 10.1007/BF01449896; G. Frobenius, S.-Ber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin (1912), 456-477.

articles.title: Perron–Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a real square matrix
with rows and columns indexed by a nonempty finite set $S$, and suppose $A$ is irreducible: its
entries are nonnegative, and for all $i, j \in S$ there is a path $i = i_0, i_1, \dots, i_k = j$ of
length $k \ge 1$ with $A_{i_{t-1} i_t} > 0$ for every $t$. Then there are a real number $r > 0$ and
a vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^S$ with $v_i > 0$ for every $i \in S$ such that $Av = rv$, and every
complex number $\mu$ with $\det(\mu E - A_{\mathbb{C}}) = 0$ satisfies $|\mu| \le r$, where $E$ is
the identity matrix and $A_{\mathbb{C}}$ is the complex matrix with the same entries as $A$.

articles.title: Complexification of a real matrix
articles.statement:
For a real square matrix $A$ with rows and columns
indexed by a nonempty finite set $S$, its complexification $A_{\mathbb{C}}$ is the complex matrix
with entries $(A_{\mathbb{C}})_{ij} = A_{ij}$ for $i, j \in S$, each real entry viewed as a
complex number.

articles.title: Determinant of the empty principal Fourier minor
articles.statement:
Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative
ring and let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity. The determinant of the principal
Fourier minor indexed by the empty subset of $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$ equals $1$.

articles.title: Determinant of a singleton principal Fourier minor
articles.statement:
Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a
commutative ring, let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let
$a \in \mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. The determinant of the principal Fourier minor indexed by $\{a\}$
equals $\zeta^{n}$, where $n \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}$ is the representative of $a^2$ in
$\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Determinant of a principal Fourier minor
articles.statement:
Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring,
let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $S$ be a finite subset of
$\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. The principal Fourier minor determinant of $S$ is the determinant in $R$
of the principal Fourier minor indexed by $S$.

articles.title: Entries of a principal Fourier minor
articles.statement:
Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $S$ be a finite subset of
$\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. For all $i, j \in S$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the principal Fourier minor
indexed by $S$ equals $\zeta^{n}$, where $n \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}$ is the representative of $ij$
in $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Principal Fourier minor
articles.statement:
Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\zeta \in R$
be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $S$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.
The principal Fourier minor indexed by $S$ is the $S \times S$ matrix over $R$ whose $(i, j)$
entry is $\zeta^{n}$, where $n \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}$ is the representative of the product $ij$
in $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Primitive root of unity data
articles.statement:
For a natural number $M$ and a commutative ring $R$, root
data of order $M$ in $R$ consists of an element $\zeta \in R$ that is a primitive $M$-th root of
unity, together with the condition $M \ge 2$.

articles.title: Trudi's formula for Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinants
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$n \ge 1$, and let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be elements of $R$ with $a_0 \ne 0$. Let $A_n$ be the
$n \times n$ matrix whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ ($0 \le i, j < n$) is $a_{i+1-j}$ if
$j \le i + 1$ and $0$ otherwise. Then

$$\det A_n = \sum_{c} (-a_0)^{n - \ell(c)} \, a_{c_1} a_{c_2} \cdots a_{c_{\ell(c)}},$$

where $c = (c_1, \dots, c_{\ell(c)})$ runs over the compositions of $n$, that is, the finite
sequences of positive integers with sum $n$, and $\ell(c)$ is the number of parts of $c$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Some Hessenberg-Toeplitz Matrices with Motzkin Number Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 26 (2023), Article 23.3.4, matrix display `DetHess` lines 146–155, Lemma `lem1` lines 157–166 with equation `Trudi` at lines 159–161 and the equivalent composition sum at lines 163–165, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL26/Shattuck/sh36.tex>.

articles.title: Trudi's formula for Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinants, general case
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
commutative ring, let $n \ge 0$, and let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be any elements of $R$. Let $A_n$
be the $n \times n$ matrix whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ ($0 \le i, j < n$) is $a_{i+1-j}$
if $j \le i + 1$ and $0$ otherwise; for $n = 0$ it is the empty matrix, whose determinant is $1$.
Then

$$\det A_n = \sum_{c} (-a_0)^{n - \ell(c)} \, a_{c_1} a_{c_2} \cdots a_{c_{\ell(c)}},$$

where $c = (c_1, \dots, c_{\ell(c)})$ runs over the compositions of $n$, that is, the finite
sequences of positive integers with sum $n$, and $\ell(c)$ is the number of parts of $c$.

No hypothesis $n \ge 1$ or $a_0 \ne 0$ is needed.

articles.title: Brioschi's formula: the case $a_0 = 1$ of Trudi's formula
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring
and let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be elements of $R$ with $a_0 = 1$. For every $n \ge 0$, the
Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant $\det A_n$ of size $n$ built from $a$ satisfies

$$\det A_n = (-1)^n \sum_\alpha (-1)^{|\alpha|} m_n(\alpha) a_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots a_n^{\alpha_n},$$

where the sum, Trudi's partition sum with weight $-1$ per part, runs over the tuples
$\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$ of nonnegative integers with
$\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \dots + n\alpha_n = n$, with $|\alpha| = \alpha_1 + \dots + \alpha_n$ and
$m_n(\alpha) = |\alpha|! / (\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_n!)$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Lemma 1 with `a_0 = 1` (the sign `D_+`).

articles.title: Trudi's formula in composition form
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be elements of $R$ and let $n \ge 0$. The Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant
$\det A_n$ of size $n$ built from $a$ satisfies

$$\det A_n = \sum_{c} (-a_0)^{n - \ell(c)} \, a_{c_1} a_{c_2} \cdots a_{c_{\ell(c)}},$$

where $c = (c_1, \dots, c_{\ell(c)})$ runs over the compositions of $n$, that is, the finite
sequences of positive integers with sum $n$, and $\ell(c)$ is the number of parts of $c$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Lemma 1 and Section 3 (the composition form of the determinant).

articles.title: Trudi's formula when $a_0 = -1$
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let
$a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be elements of $R$ with $a_0 = -1$. For every $n \ge 0$, the
Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant $\det A_n$ of size $n$ built from $a$ satisfies

$$\det A_n = \sum_\alpha m_n(\alpha) \, a_1^{\alpha_1} a_2^{\alpha_2} \cdots a_n^{\alpha_n},$$

where the sum, Trudi's partition sum with weight $1$ per part, runs over the tuples
$\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$ of nonnegative integers with
$\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \dots + n\alpha_n = n$, with $|\alpha| = \alpha_1 + \dots + \alpha_n$ and
$m_n(\alpha) = |\alpha|! / (\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_n!)$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Lemma 1 with `a_0 = -1` (the sign `D_-`).

articles.title: The $1 \times 1$ Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant
articles.statement:
For every commutative ring $R$ and every
sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ in $R$, the Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant of size $1$ built
from $a$ is $\det A_1 = a_1$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Section 2, display (1).

articles.title: The $2 \times 2$ Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant
articles.statement:
For every commutative ring $R$ and every
sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ in $R$, the Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant of size $2$ built
from $a$ is $\det A_2 = a_1^2 - a_0 a_2$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Section 2, display (1).

articles.title: Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$
be elements of $R$ and let $n \ge 0$. The Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinant $\det A_n$ is the
determinant of the $n \times n$ matrix $A_n = A_n(a_0; a_1, \dots, a_n)$ whose entry in row $i$
and column $j$ ($0 \le i, j < n$) is $a_{i+1-j}$ if $j \le i + 1$ and $0$ otherwise. Thus $a_0$
fills the superdiagonal, $a_1$ the diagonal, and every entry above the superdiagonal is $0$. For
$n = 0$ the determinant is $1$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Section 2, display (1) and the notation `D_±`.

articles.title: Trudi's partition sum as a sum over compositions
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let
$s \in R$, let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be elements of $R$ and let $n \ge 0$. Trudi's partition sum

$$\sum_\alpha s^{|\alpha|} m_n(\alpha) \, a_1^{\alpha_1} a_2^{\alpha_2} \cdots a_n^{\alpha_n},$$

taken over the tuples $\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$ of nonnegative integers with
$\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \dots + n\alpha_n = n$, where $|\alpha| = \alpha_1 + \dots + \alpha_n$ and
$m_n(\alpha) = |\alpha|! / (\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_n!)$, equals

$$\sum_c s^{\ell(c)} \, a_{c_1} a_{c_2} \cdots a_{c_{\ell(c)}},$$

where $c = (c_1, \dots, c_{\ell(c)})$ runs over the compositions of $n$, that is, the finite
sequences of positive integers with sum $n$, and $\ell(c)$ is the number of parts of $c$.

The multinomial coefficient $m_n(\alpha)$ counts the compositions of $n$ in which each part $i$
occurs $\alpha_i$ times.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Lemma 1 and the composition reading of `det(A_n)` in Section 3.

articles.title: Two values of Trudi's partition sum
articles.statement:
For an integer $s$, integers $a_1, a_2, \dots$ and
$n \ge 0$, write
$T_n(s; a) = \sum_\alpha s^{|\alpha|} m_n(\alpha) \, a_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots a_n^{\alpha_n}$ for
Trudi's partition sum, where $\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$ runs over the tuples of
nonnegative integers with $\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \dots + n\alpha_n = n$, with
$|\alpha| = \alpha_1 + \dots + \alpha_n$ and
$m_n(\alpha) = |\alpha|! / (\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_n!)$. Then $T_4(1; a) = 8$, the number of
compositions of $4$, when $a_i = 1$ for all $i$; and $T_3(-1; a) = -1 + 4 - 3 = 0$ when $a_i = i$
for all $i$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Trudi's partition sum
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $s \in R$, let $n$ be a
natural number, and let $a : \mathbb{N} \to R$ (only $a_1, \dots, a_n$ enter). Trudi's
partition sum is

$$
\sum_{\alpha} s^{|\alpha|} \, m_n(\alpha) \, a_1^{\alpha_1} a_2^{\alpha_2} \cdots a_n^{\alpha_n},
$$

where $\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$ runs over the tuples of natural numbers with
$\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \cdots + n\alpha_n = n$, $|\alpha| = \alpha_1 + \cdots + \alpha_n$, and
$m_n(\alpha) = |\alpha|! / (\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_n!)$ is the multinomial coefficient, taken in
$R$. Such a tuple records a partition of $n$ with $\alpha_i$ parts equal to $i$. For $n = 0$ the
sum has the single empty term and equals $1$.

## Sources

- Taras Goy and Mark Shattuck, *Determinants of Toeplitz-Hessenberg Matrices with Fuss-Catalan Entries*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.1.2, Lemma 1 (notation `α̃`, `|α|`, `m_n(α)`).

articles.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrices are symmetric
articles.statement:
If $A = (a_{ij})$ is a real
$(n+1) \times (n+1)$ symmetric Toeplitz matrix, with rows and columns indexed by
$\{0, \dots, n\}$, then $a_{ij} = a_{ji}$ for all $i, j$.

articles.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrices from even coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be a real
$(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$. If
$c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $c(-k) = c(k)$ for every integer $k$ and
$a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$, then $A$ is a symmetric Toeplitz matrix.

articles.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrix
articles.statement:
A real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$, with rows
and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$, is symmetric Toeplitz if there is a function
$c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $c(-k) = c(k)$ for every integer $k$ and
$a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$.

## Sources

- https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL18/Felsner/felsner2.tex

articles.title: Toeplitz matrices from coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be a real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$
matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$. If $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$
satisfies $a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$, then $A$ is a Toeplitz matrix.

articles.title: Toeplitz matrix
articles.statement:
A real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$, with rows and columns
indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$, is Toeplitz if there is a function $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$
such that $a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$. Equivalently, $A$ is constant along each of its
diagonals.

Only the values $c(k)$ with $-n \le k \le n$ enter the condition, so this is the same as asking
for real coefficients $c_{-n}, \dots, c_n$.

## Sources

- https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL18/Felsner/felsner2.tex

articles.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrices are Toeplitz
articles.statement:
Every real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ symmetric
Toeplitz matrix is a Toeplitz matrix.

articles.title: Diagonal entries of a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a set with a zero
element and $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $R$. For every natural number $i$, the
$(i, i)$ entry of the lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $a_0$.

articles.title: Entries above the diagonal of a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a set with
a zero element and $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $R$. For natural numbers $i < j$, the
$(i, j)$ entry of the lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $0$.

articles.title: Entries on and below the diagonal of a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
set with a zero element and $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $R$. For natural numbers
$j \le i$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $a_{i-j}$.

articles.title: Lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a set with a zero element $0$ and let
$a = (a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots)$ be a sequence in $R$. The lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$
is the matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is $a_{i-j}$
when $j \le i$ and $0$ when $j > i$. In particular it is constant along each diagonal and
vanishes strictly above the main diagonal.

## Sources

- Ming-Jian Ding and Jiang Zeng, "Some New Results on the Minuscule Polynomials of Type A," Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), lines 640-653. URL: <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Zeng/zeng26.tex>.

articles.title: Entries of a matrix with positive minors are positive
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a real matrix whose rows
and columns are indexed by linearly ordered sets $R$ and $C$. If $M$ has positive minors, then
$M_{ij} > 0$ for all $i \in R$ and $j \in C$; these entries are the $1 \times 1$ minors of $M$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1 (total positivity).

articles.title: Eventual log-concavity of generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers
with $p \ge 1$, $a \ge 0$ and $b > 0$, let $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the generalized hyper-Fibonacci
numbers, and let $r \ge 1$ be a natural number. Then there is a natural number $N$ such that for
every $n \ge N$ we have $W^{(r)}_{p,n} > 0$ and
$W^{(r)}_{p,n} W^{(r)}_{p,n+2} \le (W^{(r)}_{p,n+1})^2$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Corollary 10 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-cor-10`).

articles.title: Hankel determinants of generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers, let
$W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers and put $\Delta = a^2 + pab - b^2$.
For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the $(r+2) \times (r+2)$ Hankel matrix
$H_{r,n} = (W^{(r)}_{p,n+i+j})_{0 \le i, j \le r+1}$ has determinant
$\det H_{r,n} = (-1)^{n+1+\lfloor (r+3)/2 \rfloor} p^{nr+r^2} b^r \Delta$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Proposition 7, quoting Ait-Amrane et al. (`jis-2026-26.2.5-prop-7`).

articles.title: A binomial-sum formula for generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers
with $p \ne 0$, let $W_{p,n}$ denote the generalized Fibonacci sequence and $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ the
generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers. For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$ with $1 \le r \le n$, the
following identity of rational numbers holds:

$$
W^{(r)}_{p,n-r} = W_{p,n+r} - \frac{p^n}{p^{r-1}} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} \binom{n-k-1}{r-k-1} W_{p,2k+1}.
$$

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Lemma 5, identity (4), quoting Ait-Amrane et al. (`jis-2026-26.2.5-lem-5`).

articles.title: Recurrence for generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers and let
$W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers. For all natural numbers $r \ge 1$
and $n \ge 1$, $W^{(r)}_{p,n} = p W^{(r)}_{p,n-1} + W^{(r-1)}_{p,n}$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Lemma 5, identity (3), quoting Ait-Amrane et al. (`jis-2026-26.2.5-lem-5`).

articles.title: Eventual positivity of lower-order hyper-Fibonacci Toeplitz determinants
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be
integers with $p \ge 1$, $a \ge 0$ and $b > 0$, and let $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the generalized
hyper-Fibonacci numbers. For natural numbers $r$, $m$ and $n$ write $T^{(r)}_{m,n}$ for the
$m \times m$ Toeplitz matrix with entry $W^{(r)}_{p,n+i-j}$ in row $i$ and column $j$
($0 \le i, j < m$). If $r \ge 1$ and $1 \le m \le r + 1$, then there is a natural number $N$ such
that $\det T^{(r)}_{m,n} > 0$ for every $n \ge N$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Corollary 9 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-cor-9`).

articles.title: Eventual positivity of hyper-Fibonacci Toeplitz determinants
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers
with $p \ge 1$, $a \ge 0$ and $b > 0$, and let $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the generalized
hyper-Fibonacci numbers. For every natural number $m \ge 1$ there is a natural number $N$ such
that for every $n \ge N$ the $m \times m$ Toeplitz matrix with entry $W^{(m-1)}_{p,n+i-j}$ in row
$i$ and column $j$ ($0 \le i, j < m$) has positive determinant.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Theorem 8 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-thm-8`).

articles.title: Eventual total positivity of hyper-Fibonacci Toeplitz matrices
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers
with $p \ge 1$, $a \ge 0$ and $b > 0$, put $\Delta = a^2 + pab - b^2$, let $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$
denote the generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers, and let $r \ge 1$ be a natural number. For a
natural number $s$ write $T_s$ for the real $(r+2) \times (r+2)$ Toeplitz matrix with entry
$W^{(r)}_{p,s+i-j}$ in row $i$ and column $j$ ($0 \le i, j \le r+1$). If $\Delta > 0$, there is a
natural number $N$ such that $T_{2n}$ has positive minors (is totally positive) for every
$n \ge N$; if $\Delta < 0$, there is a natural number $N$ such that $T_{2n+1}$ has positive
minors for every $n \ge N$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Theorem 12 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-thm-12`).

articles.title: Eventually positive bounded-order minors of hyper-Fibonacci Toeplitz matrices
articles.statement:
Let
$p, a, b$ be integers with $p \ge 1$, $a \ge 0$ and $b > 0$, let $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the
generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers, and let $r \ge 1$ be a natural number. For a natural number
$n$ let $T_n$ be the real $(r+2) \times (r+2)$ Toeplitz matrix with entry $W^{(r)}_{p,n+i-j}$ in
row $i$ and column $j$ ($0 \le i, j \le r+1$). Then there is a natural number $N$ such that for
every $n \ge N$, every natural number $k \le r + 1$ and all strictly increasing maps
$\rho, \gamma : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, r+1\}$, the $k \times k$ submatrix
$((T_n)_{\rho(u), \gamma(v)})_{0 \le u, v < k}$ has positive determinant; that is, every minor
of $T_n$ of order at most $r + 1$ is positive.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Corollary 13 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-cor-13`).

articles.title: Initial values of generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers and let
$W^{(r)}_{p,n}$ denote the generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers. For every natural number $r$,
$W^{(r)}_{p,0} = a$ and $W^{(r)}_{p,1} = p \cdot a \cdot r + b$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1, definition (2) (initial values).

articles.title: Generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p, a, b$ be integers and let $W_{p,n}$ denote the
generalized Fibonacci sequence, with $W_{p,0} = a$, $W_{p,1} = b$ and
$W_{p,n+2} = p W_{p,n+1} + W_{p,n}$. The generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers $W^{(r)}_{p,n}$, for
natural numbers $r$ and $n$, are the integers defined by $W^{(0)}_{p,n} = W_{p,n}$ and, for
$r \ge 1$, by $W^{(r)}_{p,n} = \sum_{k=0}^{n} p^{n-k} W^{(r-1)}_{p,k}$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1, definition (2).

articles.title: $p$-Lucas numbers as a companion Lucas sequence
articles.statement:
For every integer $p$, the generalized
Fibonacci sequence $W_{p,n}$ with initial values $a = 2$ and $b = p$ (the $p$-Lucas numbers
$L_{p,n}$) is the companion Lucas sequence $V(p, -1)$: $W_{p,n} = V_n(p, -1)$ for every natural
number $n$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1, remark after recurrence (1) (`p`-Lucas numbers `L_{p,n}`).

articles.title: $p$-Fibonacci numbers as a Lucas sequence
articles.statement:
For every integer $p$, the generalized
Fibonacci sequence $W_{p,n}$ with initial values $a = 0$ and $b = 1$ (the $p$-Fibonacci numbers
$F_{p,n}$) is the Lucas sequence $U(p, -1)$: $W_{p,n} = U_n(p, -1)$ for every natural number $n$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1, remark after recurrence (1) (`p`-Fibonacci numbers `F_{p,n}`).

articles.title: Generalized $p$-Fibonacci sequence
articles.statement:
For integers $p$, $a$ and $b$, the generalized
Fibonacci sequence $(W_{p,n})_{n \ge 0}$ of integers is defined by $W_{p,0} = a$, $W_{p,1} = b$
and $W_{p,n} = p W_{p,n-1} + W_{p,n-2}$ for $n \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1, recurrence (1).

articles.title: Matrices with nonnegative minors
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be linearly ordered types and
let $M$ be a real matrix with rows indexed by $\iota$ and columns indexed by $\kappa$. Then $M$
has nonnegative minors when, for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and all strictly increasing maps
$r \colon \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \iota$ and $c \colon \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \kappa$, the
$k \times k$ submatrix $(M_{r(a), c(b)})_{a, b < k}$ has nonnegative determinant. The case
$k = 0$, the empty minor, is included.

## Sources

- Ming-Jian Ding and Jiang Zeng, "Some New Results on the Minuscule Polynomials of Type A", Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.1.2, "Total positivity of the coefficient matrix" section, definition at lines 638–639 (used by the Schoenberg–Edrei lemma, line 654), <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Zeng/zeng26.tex>.

articles.title: Gasca–Peña criterion for total positivity
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix whose
rows and columns are indexed by $0, \dots, n - 1$. Then $A$ is totally positive (has positive
minors) if and only if all its initial minors are positive: for all natural numbers $k$, $i_0$
and $j_0$ with $i_0 + k \le n$, $j_0 + k \le n$ and $i_0 = 0$ or $j_0 = 0$, the $k \times k$
submatrix of $A$ with rows $i_0, \dots, i_0 + k - 1$ and columns $j_0, \dots, j_0 + k - 1$ has
positive determinant.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Theorem 3, quoting Gasca and Peña (`jis-2026-26.2.5-thm-3`).

articles.title: Matrices with positive minors
articles.statement:
A real matrix $M$ whose rows and columns are indexed by
linearly ordered sets $R$ and $C$ has positive minors (is totally positive) when, for every
natural number $k$ and all strictly increasing maps $r : \{1, \dots, k\} \to R$ and
$c : \{1, \dots, k\} \to C$, the $k \times k$ submatrix $(M_{r(a), c(b)})_{1 \le a, b \le k}$ has
positive determinant. The case $k = 0$ is the empty minor, whose determinant is $1$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Section 1 (total positivity).

articles.title: Eventual log-concavity of hyper $p$-Fibonacci and hyper $p$-Lucas numbers
articles.statement:
Let
$p \ge 1$ be an integer and $r \ge 1$ a natural number, and let $F_{p,n}^{(r)}$ and
$L_{p,n}^{(r)}$ be the generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers $W_{p,n}^{(r)}$ with initial values
$(a, b) = (0, 1)$ and $(a, b) = (2, p)$ respectively (the hyper $p$-Fibonacci and hyper
$p$-Lucas numbers). Both sequences are eventually log-concave: there is $N$ such that for all
$n \ge N$, $F_{p,n}^{(r)} > 0$ and $F_{p,n}^{(r)} F_{p,n+2}^{(r)} \le (F_{p,n+1}^{(r)})^2$, and
there is $N'$ such that for all $n \ge N'$, $L_{p,n}^{(r)} > 0$ and
$L_{p,n}^{(r)} L_{p,n+2}^{(r)} \le (L_{p,n+1}^{(r)})^2$.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Corollary 11 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-cor-11`).

articles.title: Total positivity of hyper $p$-Fibonacci Toeplitz matrices
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ be an integer
and $r \ge 1$ a natural number, and let $F_{p,n}^{(r)}$ be the hyper $p$-Fibonacci numbers, the
generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers $W_{p,n}^{(r)}$ with initial values $a = 0$ and $b = 1$.
Consider real $(r + 2) \times (r + 2)$ matrices with rows and columns indexed by
$0, \dots, r + 1$. For all sufficiently large $n$, the Toeplitz matrix with entry
$F_{p,2n+1+i-j}^{(r)}$ in row $i$ and column $j$ is totally positive. Moreover, for all
sufficiently large $n$, the Toeplitz matrix with entry $F_{p,n+i-j}^{(r)}$ in row $i$ and
column $j$ is $\mathrm{TP}_{r+1}$: each of its minors of order at most $r + 1$ is positive.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Corollary 14 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-cor-14`).

articles.title: Total positivity of hyper $p$-Lucas Toeplitz matrices
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ be an integer and
$r \ge 1$ a natural number, and let $L_{p,n}^{(r)}$ be the hyper $p$-Lucas numbers, the
generalized hyper-Fibonacci numbers $W_{p,n}^{(r)}$ with initial values $a = 2$ and $b = p$.
Consider real $(r + 2) \times (r + 2)$ matrices with rows and columns indexed by
$0, \dots, r + 1$. For all sufficiently large $n$, the Toeplitz matrix with entry
$L_{p,2n+i-j}^{(r)}$ in row $i$ and column $j$ is totally positive. Moreover, for all
sufficiently large $n$, the Toeplitz matrix with entry $L_{p,n+i-j}^{(r)}$ in row $i$ and
column $j$ is $\mathrm{TP}_{r+1}$: each of its minors of order at most $r + 1$ is positive.

## Sources

- Abdelhak Taane, Ihab-Eddine Djellas and Mohammed Mekkaoui, *Total Positivity of Toeplitz Matrices Involving Generalized Hyper-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.2.5, Corollary 15 (`jis-2026-26.2.5-cor-15`).

articles.title: The van der Waerden permanent bound
articles.statement:
For every integer $n \ge 1$ and every doubly stochastic
real $n \times n$ matrix $A$ (nonnegative entries, every row and every column summing to $1$), the
permanent of $A$ is at least $n!/n^n$.

## Sources

- G. P. Egorychev, Adv. Math. 42 (1981), 299-305, DOI 10.1016/0001-8708(81)90044-X; D. I. Falikman, Math. Notes 29 (1981), 475-479, DOI 10.1007/BF01163285.

articles.title: The two Bernoulli formulas for the inverse of Zagier's matrix agree
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $K$, the matrices $P_K$ and $Q_K$ given by the first and second Bernoulli formulas
for the inverse of Zagier's matrix are equal: $P_K = Q_K$.

articles.title: Left inverse of Zagier's matrix
articles.statement:
For every natural number $K$, the matrix $P_K$
given by the first Bernoulli formula is a left inverse of Zagier's matrix $A_K$:
$P_K A_K = I$, where $I$ is the $(K - 1) \times (K - 1)$ identity matrix.

articles.title: First Bernoulli formula for the inverse of Zagier's matrix
articles.statement:
For a natural number $K$,
$P_K$ is the rational matrix with rows and columns indexed by $1 \le i, j \le K - 1$ (empty
when $K \le 1$) whose $(i, j)$ entry is

$$(P_K)_{ij} = \frac{2}{2i-1} \sum_{n=0}^{2K-2i} \binom{2j-1}{2K-2i-n+1} \binom{n+2i-2}{n} B_n,$$

where $B_n$ is the $n$-th Bernoulli number with $B_1 = -\frac{1}{2}$ and $\binom{m}{k} = 0$
for $k > m$.

articles.title: Second Bernoulli formula for the inverse of Zagier's matrix
articles.statement:
For a natural number $K$,
$Q_K$ is the rational matrix with rows and columns indexed by $1 \le i, j \le K - 1$ (empty
when $K \le 1$) whose $(i, j)$ entry is

$$(Q_K)_{ij} = -\frac{2}{2i-1} \sum_{n=0}^{2K-2i} \binom{2K-2j}{2K-2i-n+1} \binom{n+2i-2}{n} B_n,$$

where $B_n$ is the $n$-th Bernoulli number with $B_1 = -\frac{1}{2}$ and $\binom{m}{k} = 0$
for $k > m$.

articles.title: Zagier's matrix conjecture
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a natural number, let $B_n$ be the $n$-th
Bernoulli number with $B_1 = -\frac{1}{2}$, and let $\binom{m}{k} = 0$ for $k > m$. Let $A$,
$P$ and $Q$ be the $(K - 1) \times (K - 1)$ rational matrices, with rows and columns indexed
by $1 \le i, j \le K - 1$, whose entries are

$$A_{ij} = \binom{2K - 2j}{2i - 1} + \binom{2K - 2j}{2K - 2i},$$



$$P_{ij} = \frac{2}{2i-1} \sum_{n=0}^{2K-2i} \binom{2j-1}{2K-2i-n+1} \binom{n+2i-2}{n} B_n,$$



$$Q_{ij} = -\frac{2}{2i-1} \sum_{n=0}^{2K-2i} \binom{2K-2j}{2K-2i-n+1} \binom{n+2i-2}{n} B_n.$$

Then $P = Q$, $AP = I$ and $PA = I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix; that is, the two
Bernoulli formulas agree and give the two-sided inverse of $A$.

The source assumes $K \ge 2$. The assumption is not needed: for $K \le 1$ the matrices are
empty.

## Sources

- Yawen Ma and Lee-Peng Teo, "Another Proof of Zagier's Matrix Conjecture," Journal of Integer Sequences 25 (2022), Article 22.6.4, Theorem [Zagier's conjecture], equations (eq12) and (eq13), lines 279–285, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL25/Teo/teo4.tex

articles.title: Right inverse of Zagier's matrix
articles.statement:
For every natural number $K$, the matrix $P_K$
given by the first Bernoulli formula is a right inverse of Zagier's matrix $A_K$:
$A_K P_K = I$, where $I$ is the $(K - 1) \times (K - 1)$ identity matrix.

articles.title: Zagier's matrix
articles.statement:
For a natural number $K$, Zagier's matrix $A_K$ is the rational matrix
with rows and columns indexed by $1 \le i, j \le K - 1$ (empty when $K \le 1$) whose
$(i, j)$ entry is

$$(A_K)_{ij} = \binom{2K - 2j}{2i - 1} + \binom{2K - 2j}{2K - 2i},$$

where $\binom{m}{k} = 0$ for $k > m$.
